fact.text: Philosophers have seriously debated whether the hole in a cheese is a real thing in its own right, or just a place where cheese isn't.

heads_up: Savaitgalį daug kur šlapdriba, naktimis plikledis, pajūryje – gūsingas vėjas.
Iki pirmadienio šešiuose miestuose vyks kariuomenės dienos paradai ir rikiuotės.

lithuania.headline: Kongo DR kalinti septyni lietuviai paleisti
lithuania.summary: Rugsėjo pabaigoje Kongo DR sulaikyti ir šnipinėjimu apkaltinti septyni Lietuvos keliautojai po nuo spalio vykusių derybų ir prezidento Gitano Nausėdos pokalbio su Félixu Tshisekedi paleisti – lėktuvas iš Kinšasos pakilo vidurnaktį.
lithuania.context: Draugų grupė automobiliais keliavo po Afriką; esą jie pažeidė draudimą fotografuoti tam tikrus objektus. Apie sulaikymą viešai nebuvo skelbta, kad nepakenktų deryboms.

lithuania.headline: Mokytojų streikas skaldo tėvus ir politikus
lithuania.summary: Dalis tėvų piktinasi mokytojų streiku ir teigia, kad juo piktnaudžiaujama, o teisininkas Egidijus Kūris stojo pedagogų pusėn ir sako, kad premjeras „šovė sau į koją“.
lithuania.context: Streikas vyksta tuo metu, kai Seimas grąžino 2027 metų biudžetą Vyriausybei, o ir kitų sričių profsąjungos grasina streikais dėl atlyginimų.

lithuania.headline: Nuo gruodžio vidurio – antras traukinys į Rygą
lithuania.summary: Nuo gruodžio vidurio LTG kasdien leis antrą tiesioginį traukinį Vilnius–Ryga per Daugpilį: jis išvyks 17.40 ir Rygoje bus 22.50, o nuo gruodžio 26 d. savaitgaliais kursuos ir papildomi traukiniai į Daugpilį.
lithuania.context: Iki šiol vienintelis tiesioginis rytinis traukinys į Rygą važiuoja per Šiaulius; traukiniai į Daugpilį nekursavo nuo 2018 metų.

world.headline: AI sell-off pushes S&P 500 into correction
world.summary: The S&P 500 fell 3.7% and the Nasdaq 5.3% on Friday, erasing its 2026 gains, as investors dumped AI stocks; Nvidia lost 14% and Anthropic shares sank 8.5% towards their $83 IPO price a day after the record listing.
world.context: Big tech firms have spent more than $1 trillion on AI in the past year, feeding fears of a bubble; Democrats' midterm win in early November added to worries.

world.headline: UK and EU strike deals to rebuild post-Brexit ties
world.summary: Britain and the EU agreed deals on youth mobility, food and farm trade and emissions trading; the youth scheme will let 100,000 people each way aged 18 to 31 live, work or study abroad for up to three years, starting by January 2030.
world.context: Britain voted to leave the EU in 2016 and left in 2020, after years of bitter negotiations. Trade with the bloc became harder, and recent UK governments have sought closer ties.

world.headline: Trump threatens to penalise firms building AI data centres abroad
world.summary: Trump said US tech firms will face "tremendous penalties" if they build AI data centres abroad, claiming China would take them, but gave no details and said his own officials were hearing it for the first time.
world.context: It follows new US rules this week requiring licences to buy advanced AI chips, aimed at stopping them reaching China.

world.headline: Denmark expels Russian diplomat over alleged murder plot
world.summary: Denmark says Russian intelligence planned to kill US-Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner at a concert near Copenhagen in September with help from a banned gang, and gave Russia's defence attaché seven days to leave; Moscow calls it unsubstantiated.
world.context: Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, European countries have accused Moscow of a growing campaign of sabotage and plots on their soil. Danish intelligence says this is the first Russian assassination attempt it has seen in Denmark.

interesting.headline: Anthropic mathematician claims Riemann hypothesis proof with Claude
interesting.summary: Levent Alpöge says he spent about six weeks with a non-public version of Claude to prove the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis; the proof, written in the Lean language, runs to over 250,000 pages and Terence Tao says verification is some way off.
interesting.context: The Riemann hypothesis, about how prime numbers are distributed, carries a $1m prize.

interesting.headline: Harry Kane out for months with ankle injury
interesting.summary: England captain Harry Kane is expected to miss a few months after hurting his ankle in a collision 20 minutes into Bayern Munich's 1-1 home draw with Köln, in which Michael Olise was also injured.

interesting.headline: New 'Home Alone' sequel in the works with Macaulay Culkin
interesting.summary: Disney is developing a new Home Alone with Macaulay Culkin returning as Kevin McCallister, written by Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg; Culkin's own pitch has an adult Kevin locked out by his son setting traps.

interesting.headline: Google to switch off Assistant on smart speakers
interesting.summary: Gemini for Home will replace Google Assistant on smart speakers and displays on 2 August 2027, and the Nest app shuts on 25 January 2027 in favour of Google Home.

ongoing.title: Russia-Ukraine war
ongoing.update: Russia's biggest attack this year, 110 missiles and over 400 drones, killed at least nine people, and a Russian cruise missile crashed in Poland near drills by European troops; Poland called it a provocation and NATO scrambled jets. Zelensky called Putin a 'killer' after Trump called him a friend.
ongoing.context: Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Ukraine pushed Russian troops back from Kyiv and later from parts of the east and south, but the front has since largely stalled. Peace talks led by the US have gone back and forth while Russia keeps striking Ukrainian cities.

ongoing.title: Saudi Arabia-Houthi fighting
ongoing.update: The Saudi-led coalition intercepted three Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh, the third night of alerts, after striking Hodeidah port and Sanaa; the Houthis threatened Jeddah and other ports.
ongoing.context: The Iran-backed Houthis seized Yemen's capital Sanaa in 2014, and a Saudi-led coalition intervened in 2015 to back the government. A truce from 2022 calmed the fighting, but in recent weeks the Houthis have struck Saudi cities again, damaging Riyadh's tallest tower.

ongoing.title: US-Iran tensions
ongoing.update: Trump said Iran wants a deal but its terms are unacceptable, while US and Israel were reported to be weighing a new assault; the Pentagon says the war has cost the US $48.3bn.
ongoing.context: The US and Iran have been hostile since the 1979 revolution, with fights over Iran's nuclear programme. This year tensions turned into open war, with US strikes on Iran and Iranian attacks across the region.

ongoing.title: Nvidia CEO's affair with alleged Chinese spy
ongoing.update: Trump urged Nvidia to give Jensen Huang "a second chance" after a "big apology", though the board rules it out; the SEC is reportedly probing Nvidia's accounting and Huang agreed to testify to the Senate.
ongoing.context: Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and built it into the world's leading AI chipmaker. He resigned on 12 November after reports of affairs, including one with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy who may have helped route restricted chips to China, triggering several investigations.

ongoing.title: Protests across France and Europe
ongoing.update: Thousands of mostly young people marched in 25 European countries over living costs, housing, military spending and climate, and Italy's main union staged a strike and march in Rome.
ongoing.context: Over recent weeks protests over living costs and budget cuts have spread from France to other European countries, led largely by young people.
